rules.description: Single Choice Questions allow only one correct option; distractors should reflect common misconceptions.
Ensure appropriate tagging. Factual (Medium), Understanding (Easy/Medium/Hard), Application (Medium/Hard).
Check that tagging at chapter and sub-topic level is correct and appears twice for proper tagging.
Apply LOs based on chapter or sub-topic level relevance. Multiple LOs may be tagged if valid.
Solution must match correct option. Explanation must begin with 'The correct answer is…' and clarify incorrect options.
Ensure clarity, NCERT alignment, precision, grammatical accuracy, and British English usage.
Use 1), 2), 3), 4) format during validation. Maintain option clarity and avoid repetition.
Plausible distractors must be used. Avoid 'All of the above' or 'None' unless justified.
Use British English. Convert American spellings (e.g., color → colour).
Identify duplicates. If more than 4 similar questions exist, reject the question.
Short Answer Questions require responses within 40–50 words and are worth 3 marks.
Must be concise, relevant, and organized with complete sentences.
Factual, Inferential, Analytical, Opinion-Based, Vocabulary-Based—support with textual evidence if needed.
If question has parts, tag to the highest cognitive level. Allowed: Understanding (M/H), Application (M/H).
Ensure tagging aligns with chapter/sub-topic. Learning Outcomes not applicable.
Ensure grammar, relevance, precision, and NCERT adherence. Use British English.
Reject questions if more than 4 duplicates or similar items are found.
Long Answer Questions require 100–120 word answers with intro-body-conclusion structure. Worth 6 marks.
Character Analysis, Theme-Based, Justification-Based, Opinion-Based—must include textual support.
Tag to the highest cognitive level across sub-questions. Allowed: Understanding (M/H), Application (M/H).
Ensure correct chapter/sub-topic tagging. Learning Outcomes not applicable.
Check grammar, relevance, accuracy, formatting, and British English usage.
If more than 2 duplicates exist, reject the question.
Assertion-Reason (A/R) tests factual correctness and logical connection between two statements.
Options: A) A & R true, R explains A; B) A & R true, R doesn't explain A; C) A true, R false; D) A false, R true.
Tag to appropriate chapter/sub-topic. Cognitive Level: Application (M/H). Link to Learning Outcomes.
Begin with 'The correct answer is…' and justify why incorrect options are incorrect.
Ensure clarity, relevance, alignment, and logical connection. Questions must stimulate analysis.
Reject questions with more than 2 duplicates or 3 similar items.
Extract-based questions assess comprehension of a passage from NCERT poetry or prose. Worth 5 marks.
Use short, meaningful excerpts (4–6 lines poetry, 5–8 prose).
Include Factual, Inferential, Literary Device, Theme-Based, Vocabulary questions.
Tag to the highest cognitive level among sub-questions. Application if any are application-based.
Ensure grammar, relevance, clarity, and correct spelling (British English).
Reject if more than 2 duplicates exist.
